source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 232: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions: freeze the model revision, tokenizer, prompt and output distributions, context-length strata, decoding settings, serving engine and version, hardware, runtime, quantization algorithm, bit-width, group size, scales, calibration split, batch/concurrency policy, and cost horizon. Compare the same pre-quantization weights with identical prompts, seeds, stopping rules, request trace, SLOs, and replica policy. Report measured facts with units, and separate nominal weight storage from total runtime memory.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at fixed held-out quality and correctness, error-rate, OOM, and p99-latency gates, weight-only quantization reduces cost per accepted output token by lowering resident weight memory enough to improve feasible packing or throughput without an unreported fallback. Falsify this if any gate fails, kernel support differs, quality loss exceeds a prespecified task-level margin, or paired cost does not exceed a prespecified minimum benefit. Treat effects as workload-stratum dependent, not as one average.

Controlled experiment: checksum both artifacts and record software, driver, topology, power/thermal state, and quantization metadata. Use a held-out, leakage-audited calibration/evaluation split with per-task quality and exact correctness tests, including long contexts and failure cases. Replay the same seeded request trace after warmup across randomized alternating runs and fixed concurrency/load strata. Measure TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency (including p50/p95/p99), throughput in requests/s and accepted output tokens/s, concurrency, queueing, error/timeout/OOM rates, per-device memory by component (weights, activations, KV cache, workspace, allocator reserve), utilization, power, and cost per accepted token. Verify selected kernels and record fallback paths, numerical/output differences, and admission behavior. Use paired summaries with bootstrap or an explicitly justified confidence interval, and report stratum results and missing data.

Confounders include batching/scheduler policy, prompt and output length, cache state, kernel/autotuning, host/network contention, thermal throttling, fragmentation, calibration leakage, run order, and replica scaling. Keep a reference canary, define quality/SLO/error/OOM and minimum-benefit gates in advance, ramp gradually, and roll back to the checksummed reference on a gate breach or unexplained fallback; retain logs and redact sensitive prompts. These measurements are evidence for this workload and hardware, not a universal quantization claim.
risks: aggregate quality can hide task or long-context regressions
kernel fallback, workspace, KV cache, or fragmentation can erase nominal memory savings
batching, thermal state, workload mix, and cost-model confounding
calibration/evaluation leakage or unsupported output behavior
evidence_required: checksummed artifacts and complete software/hardware manifest
held-out per-task quality and correctness results
repeated paired latency/throughput/memory trials with units and confidence intervals
kernel support/fallback and calibration-data audit
declared cost model plus canary and rollback telemetry

source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 18: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and decision criterion: define the model graph, weights, precision, GPU count and memory, latency SLO (including p99), request and output-length distributions, concurrency, batch policy, fault/reconfiguration budget, interconnect topology and bandwidth, and software versions. Tensor parallelism (TP) splits eligible matrix operations across GPUs, requiring frequent collectives on the critical path but keeping each pipeline stage active for a request. Pipeline parallelism (PP) partitions layers, reducing replicated weights per GPU but adding stage-to-stage activation transfers and, for batching, microbatch bubbles and scheduling complexity. Do not decide from peak FLOPs alone; verify layer balance, partition constraints, communication placement, and whether the topology supports the required collectives.

Falsifiable hypothesis: under the stated latency workload, the chosen scheme meets the p99 latency and correctness gates with lower tail communication/synchronization cost and adequate per-GPU memory headroom. Falsify it if controlled replay shows a gate breach, imbalance, bubble or collective tail, reconfiguration interruption beyond budget, or unsafe memory pressure. A reasonable prior for a latency-sensitive low-batch service is TP when fast intra-node collectives and balanced sharding are available; PP becomes plausible when the model cannot fit under TP, interconnect costs favor staged transfers, or batching amortizes bubbles. This is a testable prior, not a platform fact.

Controlled experiment: implement matched TP and PP variants with the same model, precision, tokenizer, prompts, decoding, hardware placement, request trace, replicas, and warmup. Sweep realistic concurrency, prompt/output-length strata, batch and (for PP) microbatch sizes. Randomize alternating trials and measure TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end p50/p95/p99, throughput, queueing, per-GPU memory/utilization, communication bytes/time, collective wait, activation-transfer time, pipeline bubble fraction, synchronization stalls, error/timeout rate, and power/cost. Record layer-to-GPU mapping, tensor shapes, topology, NCCL/transport configuration, and reconfiguration/failure recovery time; verify outputs against a reference. Use repeated paired runs with confidence intervals and report strata rather than an aggregate that hides tails.

Confounders are placement/topology, kernel choice, overlap, scheduler and microbatch policy, sequence-length mix, warmup, thermal state, background traffic, allocator fragmentation, and different fault domains. Canary the winner with explicit p99, error, memory-headroom, and correctness gates; retain the other configuration for rollback, revert on breach, and do not claim general superiority without evidence on the target workload.
risks: TP collectives or PP activation transfers can dominate p99 tails
pipeline bubbles and layer imbalance can hide behind average throughput
topology, placement, scheduler, and microbatch confounding
fault or reconfiguration behavior may violate service SLOs
evidence_required: matched TP/PP artifacts and topology/placement manifest
repeated paired traces across concurrency and length strata
per-GPU memory, communication, bubble, tail-latency, and correctness telemetry
fault/reconfiguration timing and recovery evidence
canary SLO gates and rollback record
